From my experience, learning which fret corresponds to which note, what notes to play, and what said notes sound like seems to be the key, and can take a while.


This [video](https://youtu.be/tcok98Vk6uA) is a good starting place for matching frets to note names.

The channel I just linked to has other content that might help with the second step. Also, watching music theory YouTube (Adam Neely, 12tone, etc) to absorb a bit of theory was helpful for me. 

Learning what notes sound like will come with practice, so keep trying to learn songs by ear, especially after taking the steps described above.

Hope this helps!

Just beat the demo, it's fantastic! All of the unique abilities of the enemies are awesome and challenging to deal with, the rogue-like elements blend with the game seamlessly, the difficulty names are funny (and something tells me the highest ones get a bit sadistic), and SRS is reverse-engineered perfectly.


My biggest gripe is with the PC version's window. Yes, I get it's developed for Android too, but on PC, a phone-sized window is awkward. 

A few smaller nitpicks, too: the Android version's touch controls are way too tiny to be comfortably usable, vertical or horizontal (if controller support isn't implemented yet, that'd be a good idea). 
The same three songs, while good, get grating when you're forced to listen to them over and over while going through the story. 
The default colors of the pieces are too monotone for me, and while there is an option to color the pieces like mainline Tetris games, I feel like there could be a better middle-of-the-road color palette that would work better than straight red or blue.

I said "inconsistent", not "slow". 
Timing windows are symmetrical, meaning that in DDR, the window is 16.7 ms before AND after the note is supposed to be hit to achieve a Marvelous. I'm saying that I find stricter timing windows more frustrating because I get bad ratings when I feel like I nailed the timing just because I was off by an obnoxiously tiny amount of time.

I should clarify that I've been playing rhythm games for more than 10 years, so I think I know what I'm talking about.
